sentence: This project studies how carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus affect juvenile and adult consumers, using mathematical models and laboratory experiments.
This project studies how fire ants form rafts and bridges using simple local rules, and builds robots that follow those rules on water.
This project builds a system that lets many viewers share immersive content over a millimeter wave network.
This project studies how cells sort and transport proteins to specific regions using molecular machinery called clathrin.
This project studies how crystal vacancies and electron flow affect the densification of ceramic particles made by additive manufacturing.
This project provides a confocal microscope that lets researchers study plants, including microbial interactions and protein localization.
This project builds software that predicts the crystal forms a new drug can take, using artificial intelligence and simulation techniques.
This project prints magnetic scaffolds that copy human bone and tests whether magnetic fields can guide stem cells into bone-forming cells.
This project builds ways to protect quantum circuits on cloud-based quantum computers from attacks that leak information or give incorrect results.
This project studies how mixotrophs that photosynthesize and also ingest bacteria respond to a lack of iron and manganese.
This project studies how neurons of the trigeminal ganglion form and extend axons to their target tissues in the chick.
This project develops methods that use mass spectrometry to measure the interactions and structures of proteins and protein complexes in solution.
This project measures carbon and oxygen tracers in Arctic air samples over time to track changes in the ocean and on land.
This project studies how competition between species affects the stability of ecosystems over time, using single-celled organisms called protists in the laboratory.
This project studies how proteins and DNA behave in small water droplets in the air, using laboratory experiments and computational simulations.
This project develops a theory to identify and describe strongly entangled phases of matter from local data, in experiments and many-body simulations.
